items.bold: HEGSETH: "CEASEFIRE IS NOT OVER." Caine: Iran attacked US "10+ times" — "below threshold of restarting major combat." "Grasping at straws."
items.text: CNN (live, 4 minutes ago) and CBS News confirmed: Defense Secretary Hegseth stated at the Pentagon briefing Tuesday: "The ceasefire is not over." Project Freedom is "separate and distinct from Operation Epic Fury — defensive in nature, focused in scope and temporary in duration, with one mission: protecting innocent commercial shipping from Iranian aggression." Joint Chiefs Chair Caine: Iran has attacked US forces "more than 10 times" since the April 8 ceasefire but this "fell below the threshold of restarting major combat operations." Caine added: "It feels like Iran is grasping at straws." The ceasefire is formally confirmed as still in effect. This is the most important statement of the day — it means the US is NOT resuming full airstrikes and the war framework continues. Brent dipped slightly on ceasefire confirmation.

items.bold: FUJAIRAH FIRE: Iranian drone sparked fire at oil facility. THREE INDIAN NATIONALS WOUNDED. Modi condemned.
items.text: NPR (3 hours ago) and Business Standard confirmed: One Iranian drone sparked a fire at a key oil facility in Fujairah — the UAE's major oil terminal on the Gulf of Oman side. Three Indian nationals were wounded in the attack. UAE Defence Ministry confirmed its air defenses engaged 15 missiles and four drones fired by Iran on Monday. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia both condemned the strikes against the UAE — Saudi Arabia called on Iran to "cease these attacks, comply with principles of international law." Indian PM Narendra Modi condemned the attacks, stating: "The targeting of civilians and infrastructure is unacceptable." India stands in "firm solidarity" with the UAE and stressed "safe and uninterrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is vital for enduring regional peace, stability and global energy security."

items.bold: ARAGHCHI: Talks "MAKING PROGRESS." QALIBAF: "New equation" — Iran "yet to fully respond." Diplomatic + military both active.
items.text: CBS News and NPR confirmed: Iranian FM Araghchi said Monday that talks between the US and Iran are "making progress." He warned the US and UAE "should be wary of being dragged back into quagmire by ill-wishers." Iran's parliament speaker Qalibaf warned Tuesday that a "new equation" in the strait is taking shape and accused Washington of undermining shipping security in Hormuz through "violation of the ceasefire and imposition of a blockade." Qalibaf signalled Tehran "has yet to fully respond to the US" — suggesting Iran is preparing a next move beyond Monday's fast boats and cruise missiles. The divergence: Araghchi (FM, diplomatic track) says progress; Qalibaf (parliament, hardline) signals escalation. Both tracks running simultaneously.

assessment.body:
Tuesday 7:30 PM IST. Day 67. The ceasefire holds — for now. Three Indians are wounded. Modi has spoken.

THE PENTAGON BRIEFING — WHAT IT MEANS
• Hegseth: "The ceasefire is not over"
• Project Freedom: "separate and distinct from Operation Epic Fury — defensive, focused, temporary"
• Caine: Iran attacked US 10+ times since April 8 ceasefire — "below threshold"
• Caine: "It feels like Iran is grasping at straws"
• Full war NOT resuming — this is the most important clarity of Day 67
• Brent dipped slightly on ceasefire confirmation

THE FUJAIRAH STRIKE — INDIA'S DIRECT CASUALTY
• Iranian drone sparked fire at key Fujairah oil facility
• Three Indian nationals wounded — India's first direct war casualties
• PM Modi condemned the attacks: "Targeting civilians and infrastructure is unacceptable"
• India in "firm solidarity" with UAE
• Modi stressed Hormuz free shipping "vital for regional peace and global energy security"
• This is India's strongest statement since February 28

THE DIPLOMATIC DIVERGENCE IN IRAN
• Araghchi (FM, diplomatic): talks "making progress" — positive signal
• Qalibaf (parliament, hardline): "new equation" — Iran "yet to fully respond"
• Both tracks running — Supreme Leader must choose which path
• Araghchi's "progress" signal + Hegseth's ceasefire confirmation = space for deal exists

INDIA'S ECONOMIC CRISIS — THE NUMBERS
• FII ownership NSE: 14-year low of 16.13% — structural withdrawal
• Rs 2.28 trillion FII sales in first 4 months of 2026 — record exodus
• Brent $114: $10/bbl rise = 35bps added to India CPI + $15bn import bill
• Sensex -421. Nifty -126. Rupee 95.27
• OMC hike Rs 7-10/L imminent this week

THE INDIA ACTION REQUIRED
• Three Indian nationals wounded = political mandate to engage
• Modi's Hormuz statement = diplomatic opening to US on Project Freedom
• MEA must formally request Indian-flagged tanker inclusion in Project Freedom
• Emergency kharif fertiliser sourcing from alternate suppliers NOW

VERDICT: Day 67 closes with the ceasefire formally intact but the West Asia War in a new phase. Project Freedom is under daily Iranian attack. Iran is simultaneously signalling diplomatic progress (Araghchi) and preparing a "new equation" (Qalibaf). Three Indian nationals are wounded in Fujairah. PM Modi has condemned the attacks — India is now formally in the conflict narrative. The Trump-Xi meeting next week and China's pressure on Iran is the best remaining hope for a breakthrough. India must get its tankers into Project Freedom before Wednesday.

featured.desc: Chokepoint control is no longer binary (open/closed) but a layered spatial contest spanning seabed topology, island sovereignty, electronic warfare, and visibility asymmetry. The cartography of maritime control in the 2026 crisis.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.title: Geopolitics of Fertiliser Supply in India
featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
